items.heading: If You Are Mapping Out
items.text: If you are mapping out cloud computing career skills for India, treat it as a sequence, not a shopping list: get comfortable with Linux and networking basics, choose one cloud platform based on the job postings you actually see in your target city, build a real project inside its free tier, sit the associate-level certification for that platform once your project works, then add containers and basic CI/CD, and only after that decide whether to specialise (security, Kubernetes, cost optimisation) or add a second platform. Certificates without lab proof behind them are the single biggest reason self-taught candidates get filtered out early.

items.heading: Second
items.text: Second-largest by market share and, in a large share of Indian enterprise job postings, the platform with the most listings overall, driven by companies already running Microsoft 365 and on-premise Windows infrastructure.

items.heading: None of the Three Major
items.text: None of the three major platforms is objectively "the best", they win in different situations, and the right pick depends on your target city, target industry, and how much of your learning time you can realistically commit right now.

rows: Largest global market share and the broadest set of services (200+), which usually translates to the widest range of job postings in India, especially in Bengaluru.
Widest ecosystem, most third-party training material, most community support for troubleshooting.
Breadth can be a downside for a beginner, the sheer number of services makes it easy to spread learning too thin.

Smallest of the three in India by job volume, but the fastest-growing by percentage, concentrated in data-heavy and AI-heavy companies using BigQuery, Kubernetes (GKE), and Google's AI infrastructure.
Strong choice if the target direction is data engineering, analytics, or Kubernetes specifically, GCP is considered the strongest platform for Kubernetes work.
Fewer total openings means less flexibility if you need to change employers quickly in a smaller city.

visuals.heading: Deploy Something Small But Complete

items.heading: Deploy Something Small But Complete
items.text: Deploy something small but complete inside the free tier: a website with a database, a backup routine, or a simple automated pipeline, not just a single virtual machine that does nothing.

items.heading: Break IT on Purpose
items.text: Break it on purpose. Turn off a service, misconfigure a permission, or simulate a failure, then fix it and write down what you learned. This is closer to real on-the-job troubleshooting than any exam question.

items.heading: Track and Control the Cost
items.text: Track and control the cost of your own lab. Employers increasingly expect cloud staff to understand billing and cost optimisation, not just how to spin resources up.

items.heading: Document the Project the Way
items.text: Document the project the way an engineer would explain it in an interview: the problem, the setup, what broke, and how you fixed it, not just a list of services used.
